vsm2.14:81.1:
81. Among the remaining aggregates, however, whatever has the characteristic of being felt should be understood,
all taken together, as the feeling aggregate; and whatever has the characteristic of perceiving, all taken together,
as the perception aggregate; and whatever has the characteristic of forming, all taken together, as the formations
aggregate; and whatever has the characteristic of cognizing, all taken together, as the consciousness aggregate.
vsm2.14:81.2:
Herein, since the rest are easy to understand when the consciousness aggregate has been understood,
we shall therefore begin with the commentary on the consciousness aggregate.
vsm2.14:82.1:
82. "Whatever has the characteristic of cognizing should be understood, all taken together,
as the consciousness aggregate" was said above.
vsm2.14:82.2: And what has the characteristic of cognizing (vijānana)?
vsm2.14:82.3: Consciousness (viññāṇa); according as it is said, "It cognizes, friend, that is why 'consciousness' is said" (M I 292).
vsm2.14:82.4: The words viññāṇa (consciousness), citta (mind, consciousness), and mano (mind) are one in meaning.
vsm2.14:82.5:
That same consciousness, though one in its individual essence with the characteristic of cognizing,
is threefold according to kind, namely, (I) profitable, (II) unprofitable, and (III) indeterminate.
vsm2.14:83.1:
THE 89 KINDS OF CONSCIOUSNESS—SEE TABLE III I. Herein, the profitable is fourfold according to plane, namely,
(A) of the sense sphere, (B) of the fine-material sphere, (C) of the immaterial sphere, and (D) supramundane.
vsm2.14:83.2:
I. A. Herein, (1)–(8) that of the sense sphere is eightfold, being classified according to joy,
equanimity, knowledge, and prompting, that is to say: (1) when accompanied-by-joy it is either
associated-with-knowledge and unprompted, or (2) prompted; or (3) it is dissociated-from-knowledge and likewise
unprompted, or (4) prompted; and (5) when accompanied-by-equanimity it is either associated-with-knowledge and prompted, or (6)
unprompted; or (7) it is dissociated-from-knowledge and likewise unprompted, or (8) prompted.
vsm2.14:84.1:
84. (1) When a man is happy on encountering an excellent gift to be given, or recipient, etc., or some such cause for joy, and by
placing right view foremost that occurs in the way beginning "There is merit in giving" (M I 288), he unhesitatingly and unurged by
others performs such merit as giving, etc., then his consciousness is accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, and unprompted.
vsm2.14:84.2:
(2) But when a man is happy and content in the way aforesaid, and, while placing right view foremost, yet he does it hesitantly
through lack of free generosity, etc., or urged on by others, then his consciousness is of the same kind as the last but prompted;
vsm2.14:84.3: for in this sense "prompting" is a term for a prior effort exerted by himself or others.
vsm2.14:85.1:
85. (3) But when young children have a natural habit due to seeing the behaviour of relatives and are joyful on seeing
bhikkhus and at once give them whatever they have in their hands or pay homage, then the third kind of consciousness arises.
vsm2.14:85.2:
(4) But when they behave like this on being urged by their relatives, "Give;
pay homage," then the fourth kind of consciousness arises.
vsm2.14:85.3:
(5)–(8) But when the consciousnesses are devoid of joy in these four instances through encountering
no excellence in the gift to be given, or in the recipient, etc., or through want of any such cause for joy,
then the remaining four, which are accompanied by equanimity, arise.
vsm2.14:85.4:
So sense-sphere profitable consciousness should be understood as of eight kinds,
being classed according to joy, equanimity, knowledge, and prompting.
vsm2.14:86.1: 86. I. B. The consciousness of the fine-material sphere is fivefold, being classed according to association with the jhāna factors.
vsm2.14:86.2:
That is to say, (9) the first is associated with applied thought, sustained thought, happiness, bliss, and concentration,
(10) the second leaves out applied thought from that, (11) the third leaves out sustained thought from that, (12) the fourth
makes happiness fade away from that, (13) the fifth is associated with equanimity and concentration, bliss having subsided.
vsm2.14:87.1: 87. I. C. That of the immaterial sphere is fourfold by association with the four immaterial states;
vsm2.14:87.2:
for (14) the first is associated with the jhāna of the base consisting of boundless space in the way aforesaid, while (15)–(17)
the second, third, and fourth, are respectively associated with those of the base consisting of boundless consciousness, and so on.
vsm2.14:88.1: 88. I. D. The supramundane is fourfold (18)–(21) by association with the four paths.
vsm2.14:88.2: So firstly, profitable consciousness itself is of twenty-one kinds.
vsm2.14:89.1: 89. II. The unprofitable is one kind according to plane, being only of the sense sphere.
vsm2.14:89.2: It is of three kinds according to root, as (a) rooted in greed, (b) rooted in hate, and (c) rooted in delusion.
vsm2.14:90.1:
90. II. (a) Herein, (22)–(29) that rooted in greed is of eight kinds, being classed
according to joy, equanimity, false view, and prompting,
vsm2.14:90.2:
that is to say: (22) when accompanied by joy it is either associated-with-false-view and unprompted, or (23)
prompted; or (24) it is dissociated-from-false-view and likewise unprompted or (25) prompted; and (26) when
accompanied-by-equanimity it is either associated-with-false-view and unprompted, or (27) prompted; or (28)
it is dissociated-from- false-view and likewise unprompted, or (29) prompted.
vsm2.14:91.2: when it is with consciousness that is sluggish and urged on, then it is the second kind (24).
vsm2.14:91.3:
But when a man is happy and content only, without placing wrong view foremost, and indulges in sexual
intercourse, or covets others' good fortune, or steals others' goods, with consciousness that in its own
individual essence is eager without being urged, then it is the third kind (25).
vsm2.14:91.4: When it is with consciousness that is sluggish and urged on, then it is the fourth kind (26)–(29).
vsm2.14:91.5:
But when the consciousnesses are devoid of joy in these four instances through encountering no excellence in the sense
desires, or through want of any such cause for joy, then the remaining four, which are accompanied by equanimity, arise.
vsm2.14:91.6:
So that rooted in greed should be understood as of eight kinds, being classed
according to joy, equanimity, false view and prompting.
vsm2.14:92.1:
92. II. (b) That rooted in hate is of two kinds: (30)–(31) being accompanied-by-grief
and associated-with-resentment, it is either prompted or unprompted.
vsm2.14:92.2:
It should be understood to occur at the times when consciousness is either keen if
unprompted or sluggish if prompted in the killing of living things, and so on.
vsm2.14:93.1:
93. II. (c) That rooted in delusion is of two kinds: (32)–(33) being accompanied-by-equanimity,
it is either associated-with uncertainty or associated-with-agitation.
vsm2.14:93.2: It should be understood to occur at the time of indecision or of distraction.
vsm2.14:93.3: So unprofitable consciousness is of twelve kinds.
vsm2.14:94.1: 94. III. The indeterminate is of two kinds: (i) resultant and (ii) functional.
vsm2.14:94.2:
Herein, III. i. resultant is of four kinds according to plane; namely, (A) of the sense sphere,
(B) of the fine-material sphere, (C) of the immaterial sphere, and (D) supramundane.
vsm2.14:94.3: Herein, III. i. A. that of the sense sphere is of two kinds, namely, (a) profitable result and (b) unprofitable result.
vsm2.14:94.4: And III. i. A. (a) the profitable resultant is of two kinds, namely, (1) without root-cause and (2) with root-cause.
vsm2.14:95.1: 95. III. i. A. (a) i. Herein, that without root-cause is that devoid of non-greed, etc., as the cause of result.
vsm2.14:95.2:
It is of eight kinds as (34) eye-consciousness (35)–(38), ear-, nose-, tongue-, and body-consciousness (39), mind-element
with the function of receiving (40)–(41), the two mind-consciousness-elements with the functions of investigating, and so on.
vsm2.14:96.1: 96. Herein, (34) eye-consciousness has the characteristic of being supported by the eye and cognizing visible data.
vsm2.14:96.2: Its function is to have only visible data as its object.
vsm2.14:96.3: It is manifested as occupation with visible data.
vsm2.14:96.4: Its proximate cause is the departure of (70) the functional mind-element that has visible data as its object.
vsm2.14:96.5:
(35)–(38) Ear-, nose-, tongue-, and body-consciousness respectively have the characteristic
of being supported by the ear, etc., and of cognizing sounds, and so on.
vsm2.14:96.6: Their functions are to have only sounds, etc., as their respective objects.
vsm2.14:96.7: They are manifested as occupation with respectively sounds, and so on.
vsm2.14:96.8: Their proximate cause is the departure of (70) the functional mind-element that has respectively sounds, etc., as its object.
vsm2.14:97.1:
97. (39) The resultant mind-element has the characteristic of cognizing respectively visible data,
etc., immediately next to (34)–(38) eye-consciousness, and so on.
vsm2.14:97.2: Its function is to receive visible data, and so on.
vsm2.14:97.3: It is manifested as the state of receiving corresponding to that last-mentioned function.
vsm2.14:97.4: Its proximate cause is the departure of eye-consciousness, and so on.
vsm2.14:97.5:
(40)–(41) Also the twofold resultant mind-consciousness-element without root- cause with the function of investigating,
etc., has as its characteristic the cognizing of the six kinds of objects.
vsm2.14:97.6: Its function is that of investigating, and so on.
vsm2.14:97.7: It is manifested as the state of investigating corresponding to that last-mentioned function.
vsm2.14:97.8: Its proximate cause is the heart-basis.
vsm2.14:98.1:
98. But it is classed according to its association with joy or with equanimity, and according to its being divisible
into that with two positions and that with five positions in the cognitive series.
vsm2.14:98.2:
For of these, (40) one is associated-with-joy because of its presence when entirely desirable objects occur; and it has two
positions in the cognitive series because it occurs as investigating at the five doors and as registration at the end of impulsion.
vsm2.14:98.3:
(41) The other kind is associated-with-equanimity because of its presence when desirable-neutral objects occur, and it
has five positions since it occurs as investigation, registration, rebirth-linking, life-continuum, and death.
vsm2.14:99.1:
99. And this eightfold resultant consciousness without root-cause is of two kinds as well
because of having an invariable object and a variable object.
vsm2.14:99.2: It is of three kinds as classed according to bodily pleasure, mental joy, and equanimity.
vsm2.14:99.3:
For (34)–(38) the five consciousnesses have each an invariable object since they occur respectively
only with respect to visible data, and so on. The others (39)–(41) have a variable object.
vsm2.14:99.4:
For here (39) the mind-element occurs with respect to the five beginning with visible data, and (40)–(41)
the two mind-consciousness-elements occur with respect to all six.
vsm2.14:99.5:
Here, however, body-consciousness is associated with bodily pleasure. The mind-consciousness-element
(40) with two positions is associated with mental joy; the other (41) is associated with equanimity.
vsm2.14:99.6: So firstly, the profitable resultant without root-cause should be understood as of eight kinds.
vsm2.14:100.1:
100. But that with root-cause is (42)–(49) that associated with non-greed, etc., as the cause of the result.
It is of eight kinds because it is classed according to joy, etc., like the profitable of the sense sphere (1)–(8).
vsm2.14:100.2: But it does not occur with respect to the six objects through giving, etc., as the profitable does;
vsm2.14:100.3:
for it occurs only with respect to the six objects that are included among limited states,
as rebirth-linking, life-continuum, death, and registration.
vsm2.14:100.4: But the prompted and unprompted states should be understood here as due to the source it has come from, and so on.
vsm2.14:100.5:
And while there is no difference in the associated states, the resultant should be understood as passive
like the reflection of a face in a looking-glass while the profitable is active like the face.
vsm2.14:101.1:
101. III. i. A. (b) Unprofitable resultant, though, is without root-cause only. It is of seven kinds as (50) eye-consciousness,
(51)–(54) ear-, nose-, tongue-, and body-consciousness, (55) mind-element with the function of receiving, and (56)
mind-consciousness-element with the function of investigating, etc., and having five positions.
vsm2.14:101.2: It should be understood as to characteristic, etc., in the same way as the profitable resultant without root-cause (34)–(41).
vsm2.14:102.1:
102. Profitable resultant, though, has desirable or desirable-neutral objects only,
while these have undesirable or undesirable-neutral objects only.
vsm2.14:102.2:
The former are of three kinds, being classed according to equanimity, bodily pleasure, and mental joy,
while these are of two kinds, being classed according to bodily pain and equanimity.
vsm2.14:102.3: For here it is only body-consciousness that is accompanied by bodily pain; the rest are accompanied by equanimity.
vsm2.14:102.4:
And the equanimity in these is inferior, and not very sharp as the pain is; while in the former
it is superior, and not very sharp as the pleasure is.
vsm2.14:102.5:
So with these seven kinds of unprofitable resultant and the previous sixteen kinds of profitable
resultant, sense-sphere resultant consciousness is of twenty-three kinds.
vsm2.14:103.1: 103. III. i. B. That of the fine-material sphere, however, is of five kinds (57)–(61) like the profitable (9)–(13).
vsm2.14:103.2:
But the profitable occurs in a cognitive series with the impulsions as an attainment of jhāna, while this
occurs in an existence in the fine-material sphere as rebirth-linking, life-continuum, and death.
vsm2.14:104.1:
104. III. i. C. And as that of the fine-material sphere was like the profitable of that sphere so
that of the immaterial sphere (62)–(65) is of four kinds like the profitable too (14)–(17).
vsm2.14:104.2: And its occurrence is classed in the same way as that of the fine-material sphere.
vsm2.14:105.1:
105. III. i. D. The supramundane resultant is of four kinds (66)–(69) because it is respectively
the fruitions of the consciousnesses associated with the four paths (18)–(21).
vsm2.14:105.2: It occurs in two ways, that is to say, as fruition in the cognitive series of the path and as fruition attainment (see Ch. XXII).
vsm2.14:105.3: So resultant consciousness in all the four planes is of thirty-six kinds.
vsm2.14:106.1:
106. III. ii. The functional, however, is of three kinds according to plane: (A) of the sense sphere,
(B) of the fine-material sphere, (C) of the immaterial sphere.
vsm2.14:106.2: Herein, III. ii. A., that of the sense sphere, is of two kinds, namely, (1) without root-cause, and (2) with root-cause.
vsm2.14:106.3:
III. ii. A. 1. Herein, that without root-cause is that devoid of non-greed, etc., as the cause of result.
That is of two kinds, being classed as (70) mind-element, and (71)–(72) mind-consciousness-element.
vsm2.14:107.1:
107. Herein, (70) the mind-element has the characteristics of being the forerunner of eye-consciousness,
etc., and of cognizing visible data and so on.
vsm2.14:107.3: It is manifested as confrontation of visible data, and so on.
vsm2.14:107.4: Its proximate cause is the interruption of the continued occurrence of consciousness as life-continuum.
vsm2.14:107.5: It is associated with equanimity only.
